chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what He made permissible for them therein.
To lead astray those who follow them.
That is, to take them to the Hellfire.
ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's power over faithful believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority over believers is not absolute but contingent upon divine permission, serving as a test to distinguish the steadfast from the negligent. This limited dominion (*sulṭān*) allows Satan to incite misguidance toward Hellfire, yet he cannot compel faith or force obedience, preserving human free will within the Shia theological framework of *amr bayn al-amrayn*.
